moved.sentence: **High internal coupling ratio (>0.6) = strong scope group candidate.** If 80% of a directory's imports are within the same directory, it is self-contained.

judged.note: should-treat-high-coupling-ratio-as-candidate keeps the >0.6 threshold and strong-candidate call; the rationale keeps the 80%-internal-imports example and self-contained reason.

moved.sentence: **Low coupling ratio (<0.3) = likely belongs elsewhere.** A file that imports mostly from other directories is probably a leaf consumer or a shared utility — consider merging it into the scope group it depends on most.

judged.note: should-consider-merging-low-ratio-files keeps the <0.3 threshold, likely-belongs-elsewhere and merge-into-most-depended-on group; the rationale keeps the leaf-consumer or shared-utility explanation.

moved.sentence: **Unidirectional dependency = separate scope groups.** If layer A only imports layer B (never the reverse), A and B are separate concerns even if they live near each other.

judged.note: should-separate-unidirectional-layers keeps the A-only-imports-B condition and separate groups even when near each other; the rationale keeps the separate-concerns reason.

moved.sentence: **High fan-in files are shared infrastructure.** A file imported by 10+ other files across multiple candidate groups is a cross-cutting dependency — flag it for `cross-cutting-detection` rather than assigning it to one group.

judged.note: should-flag-high-fan-in-files keeps the 10+ importers across multiple groups condition and flag-for-cross-cutting-detection rather than assign; the rationale keeps the cross-cutting-dependency claim.

moved.sentence: **Circular dependencies force co-location.** Files in a cycle must remain in the same scope group until the cycle is resolved.

judged.note: must-co-locate-cyclic-files keeps the MUST stay in one group until the cycle is resolved and the force-co-location headline.

moved.sentence: Document the cycle as a refactoring target.

judged.note: should-document-cycles-as-refactoring-targets keeps documenting each cycle as a refactoring target, at SHOULD.

moved.sentence: **Star imports inflate apparent coupling.** A `import com.example.util.*` may only use one symbol — do not count star imports as full coupling without verifying symbol usage.

judged.note: should-not-count-star-imports-as-full-coupling keeps the inflation claim and the verify-symbol-usage condition; the rationale keeps the one-symbol example.
